title: He survived both atomic bombs

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: This man survived both atomic bombs: Tsutomu Yamaguchi.
beats.visual: PD photo of the Hiroshima atomic cloud, slow push-in; name card types in

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: August 1945: the Mitsubishi engineer, 29, was in Hiroshima on business.
beats.visual: Sketch map of Japan: briefcase icon travels from Nagasaki to Hiroshima

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; ruler appears on the map

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About three kilometres away. Burned, temporarily blind and deaf. But there was a problem. Home was Nagasaki.
beats.visual: Rings around Hiroshima with '3 km' marker; bandage icon; map pans to Nagasaki

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; arrow back to Nagasaki

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The next day. On August 9, bandaged, he described Hiroshima to his boss.
beats.visual: Sketch office with drawing boards; speech bubble with a mushroom-cloud doodle

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: No. Then Nagasaki's bomb fell, again about three kilometres away. He survived again.
beats.visual: PD photo of the Nagasaki cloud from Koyagi-jima; second '3 km' ring

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 2009, Japan officially recognised him for both. He campaigned against nuclear weapons until he died at 93.
beats.visual: Stamp '2009' on a document; dates 1916-2010; no likeness

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: One man, two atomic bombs. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Both cloud photos side by side fade to paper; History Sketches corner logo

description: Tsutomu Yamaguchi was on a business trip in Hiroshima on August 6, 1945, then went home to Nagasaki just before the second bomb. In 2009 Japan officially recognised him as a survivor of both. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #ww2 #japan
